claim.claim-text: 1. A sheathing device (60) for guiding insertion and extraction of a bougie (10) into and from a stomach (A) during a sleeve gastroplasty, the sheathing device (60) comprising a tubular body having a main elongated lumen for slidably receiving the bougie (10) therein, and the tubular body being translatable with respect to the bougie between:

a first position in which the tubular body at least covers a guiding segment (120) of the bougie (10) during insertion and extraction of the guiding segment (120) into and from the stomach, and a second position in which the tubular body is staggered with respect to the guiding segment (120) for allowing the guiding segment (120) to serve as guide to form a sleeve within the stomach (A).
2. The sheathing device of claim 1, comprising an actuator which is configured to displace the tubular body between the first position and the second position along the bougie.

3. The sheathing device (60) of claim 1 or 2, wherein the tubular body has a proximal portion made of a first material and a distal portion made of a second material, the second material having an enhanced rigidity in comparison to the first material, said distal portion enclosing the guiding segment (120) of the bougie (10) when the tubular body is in the first position.
4. The sheathing device (60) of any one of claims 1 to 3, wherein the tubular body is made of a material which is flexible enough to bend according to the movements of the bougie (10).

5. The sheathing device (60) of any one of claims 1 to 4, wherein the tubular body comprises distal and proximal tube segments (61, 62), the proximal tube segment (62) being translatable with respect to the bougie (10) in a backward direction to expose the guiding segment (120), and the distal tube segment (61) being translatable with respect to the bougie (10) in a forward direction to hide the guiding segment (120).

6. The sheathing device (60) of any one of claims 1 to 5, wherein the actuator is a wire system comprising at least one wire (63) which is pullable to actuate translation of the sheathing device (60) with respect to the bougie (10).

7. The sheathing device (60) of any one of claims 1 to 4, wherein the tubular body extends along the bougie (10) from the stomach (A) and further along the oesophagus (B) so as to be actuated from an oral cavity of a patient.

8. A method of performing a sleeve gastroplasty using an assembly comprising a bougie (10) having a guiding segment (120) for forming the sleeve (G) and a sheath (G) for securing the guiding segment (120), the method comprising:

9. The method of claim 8, comprising extending a portion (14) of the guiding segment (120) outwardly from the lesser curve (C) of the stomach until a distal end of the portion (14) of the guiding segment (120) is located proximal to a gastroesophageal junction, and wherein the joining of the opposed walls of the stomach (B) is performed along an inner edge of the guiding segment (120) until reaching the distal end thereof, thereby defining a fluid passage between the sleeve (G) and a bypass portion (F) in a top region of the stomach (B).

10. The method of claim 8, comprising extending a portion (14) of the guiding segment (120) outwardly from the lesser curve (C) of the stomach (B) until a distal end of the portion (14) of the guiding segment (120) is located proximal to a gastroduodenal junction, and wherein the joining of the opposed walls of the stomach is performed along an inner edge of the bougie (10) until reaching the distal end thereof, thereby defining a fluid passage between the sleeve (G) and a bypass portion (F) in a distal region of the stomach (B).

11. The method of claim 9 or 10, wherein the displacement of the sheath (60) with respect to the bougie (10) in the backward direction to expose the guiding segment (120) actuates the extension of the portion (14) of the guiding segment.

12. The method of any one of claims 9 to 11, comprising retracting the portion (14) of the guiding segment (120) in alignment with the lesser curve (C) of the stomach (B) before displacing the sheath (60) with respect to the bougie (10) in the forward direction to cover the guiding segment (120).

13. The method of any one of claims 9 to 12, comprising controlling movement of the portion (14) of the guiding segment (120) with at least one wire (63) or magnet cooperating with the distal end of said portion (14).

14. The method of any one of claims 8 to 13, wherein displacing the sheath (60) is performed from an oral cavity of the patient by direct pushing and/or pulling of a wire system operatively connected to the sheath (60).
15. The method of any one of claims 8 to 13, wherein displacing the sheath (60) is performed from an oral cavity of the patient by direct pushing or pulling of the sheath (60) itself.
